desc: Parse input: read N, M, S_x, S_y, house coordinates, and move instructions.
Preprocess houses: build two dictionaries (`by_y` mapping Y to sorted list of Xs, `by_x` mapping X to sorted list of Ys).
Initialize Fenwick trees for each line in `by_y` and `by_x` to track visited houses efficiently.
Initialize current position (cx, cy) = (S_x, S_y) and a set `visited_houses` to keep track of distinct houses passed.
Determine the new position (nx, ny) based on direction and distance.
Identify the segment from (cx, cy) to (nx, ny).
If horizontal (same Y), use `by_y[cy]` and its Fenwick tree to find all unvisited houses with that Y and X in [min(cx, nx), max(cx, nx)].
If vertical (same X), use `by_x[cx]` and its Fenwick tree to find all unvisited houses with that X and Y in [min(cy, ny), max(cy, ny)].
For each house found, add its coordinate to `visited_houses` and mark it as visited in the corresponding Fenwick tree.
Print final position (cx, cy) and the size of `visited_houses`.
